title: GPG, DID and FIDO2 claims all masquerade as TrustDomain::SshLocal
description:
TrustDomain (persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:31-49) models six distinct domains, including a PgpLocal variant. Three attestors ignore it and stuff unrelated identity types into SshLocal:

- persona-attestors/src/gpg.rs:90       SpiffeId::new(TrustDomain::SshLocal, format!("gpg/{short_fp}"))  — despite TrustDomain::PgpLocal existing at spiffe_id.rs:48 and rendering as "pgp.local"
- persona-attestors/src/did_key.rs:70   SpiffeId::new(TrustDomain::SshLocal, format!("did/{short}"))    — despite TrustDomain::PersonalDid existing at spiffe_id.rs:38
- persona-attestors/src/fido2.rs:88     SpiffeId::new(TrustDomain::SshLocal, format!("fido2/{path_hash}"))

What goes wrong: the trust domain is the authority component of the SPIFFE URI and is the key the trust bundle store is indexed by (trust_bundle.rs:37, keyed on trust_domain.to_string()). Collapsing four unrelated key types into "ssh.local" means:
- an Iaa3 hardware FIDO2 identity and an Iaa1 self-asserted SSH key are issued under the same authority, so a relying party cannot distinguish them by trust domain and must string-match the path prefix instead;
- all four share one trust bundle entry, so they cannot ever be federated or revoked independently;
- the enum documents an intent the code contradicts, which is the kind of thing a contributor copies into the next attestor.

Rewrite: gpg.rs:90 → TrustDomain::PgpLocal; did_key.rs:70 → TrustDomain::PersonalDid(<the did>). FIDO2 has no matching variant — either add one or write a ponytail: comment at fido2.rs:88 stating that SshLocal is a deliberate placeholder and what it becomes. Right now nothing distinguishes 'deliberate' from 'nearest variant to hand'.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.93 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
